title: Assistant Electrician
entryRoutes: 9th grade pass with 1 Year of experience Relevant
8th grade pass with 2 Years of experience Relevant
5th grade pass with 5 Years of experience Relevant
Previous relevant Qualification of NSQF Level 2 (Helper Electrician) with 3 Years of experience Relevant Experience

quotes.text: The passing percentage for the QP will be 70%. To pass the Qualification Pack.
quotes.source: CON/Q0602 v4.0, Assessment Guidelines, item b, page 46

quotes.text: Minimum Aggregate Passing % at QP Level : 50
Min. passing marks out of 70: 49 for each NOS; 343/490 to pass the practical observation
quotes.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), grading criteria for practical observation, pages 6 and 11

passRule.note: The QP states both 70% and a 50% aggregate. The tool shows both and applies the rule the awarding body confirms; it never decides a pass on its own.

notes: Text of every NOS, element and PC is extracted from the official PDF by tools/extract_qp.py.

Observables are adapted from the CSDCI Assessment Guide for Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), whose observation checklist covers the same activities under older PC numbers. Anchors follow the WorldSkills judgement scale (0 below industry standard, 1 meets, 2 meets and in specific respects exceeds, 3 wholly exceeds and excellent).
Measurement items use only bands with a named source.

nos.title: Handle hand and power tools relevant to construction electrical works

elements.title: Handle hand/power tools for electrical works.

pcs.text: perform basic checks on power tools prior to use
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or starts the tool without looking at cable, plug, guard or bit, or uses one with visible damage.
Meets standard: checks cable, plug, switch, guard and bit before use and runs the tool briefly; does not use a faulty tool.
Exceeds in places: makes all basic checks in a set order and also confirms the bit or blade suits the material and is held tight.
Excellent: quick, complete checks as a habit; explains each check, tags and reports a faulty tool and keeps it out of use.
observables: Cable, plug and switch of the power tool are checked and undamaged before use
Safety guard is in place on the machine
Blade or drill bit is checked, in good condition and fitted firmly
Tool is run briefly to confirm it works normally before the job starts
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: handle hand/power tools for establishing/ terminating electrical connections as per requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses wrong or damaged tools (pliers on screws, knife cutting into copper), or works on a live connection.
Meets standard: picks suitable tools for stripping, tightening and crimping, uses them correctly and makes a sound connection without damage.
Exceeds in places: uses each tool cleanly with no nicked strands or chewed screw heads, and packs and shifts power tools safely.
Excellent: fluent, safe tool use throughout; connections neat and tight first time, tools kept in order and use explained to a helper.
observables: Uses the right tool for each step: stripper for insulation, matching screwdriver for terminal screws, crimper for lugs
Holds tools by their insulated handles and keeps fingers clear of blades and bits
Packs and carries power tools unplugged, with the cable coiled, in a box or case
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: use appropriate tools to trace out short circuits/faults and leakages in electrical wiring
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or tests with supply on in a resistance range, guesses by swapping parts, or cannot locate the fault.
Meets standard: isolates the circuit, uses a suitable tester or meter correctly and locates the short or leakage to a section or point.
Exceeds in places: works section by section in a logical order, finds the exact faulty spot quickly and explains how the fault occurred.
Excellent: systematic, safe and quick; confirms the fault, explains cause and fix, and retests after repair to prove it is cleared.
observables: Switches off and isolates the circuit before continuity, resistance or insulation checks
Uses a tester, multimeter or megger to locate the fault, not trial and error
Checks the circuit section by section and points out the faulty spot
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: use measuring instruments to measure size and dimension of wires, conduits as per electrical installation or maintenance work requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses the wrong instrument, misreads the scale, or gives sizes with no unit or far from the actual.
Meets standard: uses Vernier calliper and tape correctly and gives sizes close to the actual, with units, matching the job requirement.
Exceeds in places: repeats readings to confirm them, reads the Vernier scale correctly and links each size to the right conduit or wire.
Excellent: precise, quick readings every time; explains the Vernier reading and spots a wrong size of wire or conduit by measuring.
observables: Measures conduit, cable or box size with a Vernier calliper or measuring tape
Calliper jaws or tape are held square and straight on the item
Reads and states each measurement with its unit and matches it to the required size
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: use hand/ power tools to cut, and bend wire and conduit as per electrical installation or maintenance work requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cuts are crooked or burred, conduit is kinked, cracked or flattened at bends, or wire is cut short.
Meets standard: cuts conduit and wire to the needed length with square ends, deburrs, and makes smooth bends without kinks.
Exceeds in places: cuts and bends match the marked lengths and angles closely, bends are uniform and wire has neat spare length.
Excellent: clean, accurate cuts and even bends that fit first time with no waste; ends deburred and work area left tidy.
observables: Cuts conduit square with a hacksaw and removes burrs from the cut end
Cuts wire to length with cutting pliers without damaging the conductor
Bends PVC conduit with a bending spring into a smooth bend with no kink or flattening
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: use appropriate tools to splice wires by stripping insulation from terminal leads and twisting wires together
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or copper is nicked or cut, the joint is loose or untwisted, or bare copper is left exposed.
Meets standard: strips the right length cleanly, makes a tight twisted joint and insulates it fully so no copper shows.
Exceeds in places: joint is neat and holds firm when pulled, strip length is exact and taping is even and overlapping.
Excellent: splices fast and flawlessly, picks the right joint type for the job, and explains why a poor joint heats up.
observables: Strips insulation with a stripper or splicer without nicking the copper
Twists the conductors together tightly and evenly with no loose strands
Finished joint is fully covered with insulation tape or a connector, no bare copper visible
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: use appropriate hand/power tools to thread conduit ends, connect couplings, and fabricate and secure conduit support brackets
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or threads are torn or short, couplings loose or misaligned, or brackets so loose the conduit moves.
Meets standard: cuts clean threads, fits couplings tight and in line, and fixes brackets firmly so the conduit is secure.
Exceeds in places: deburrs the ends, threads only as long as needed, and brackets are level, evenly spaced and neatly fixed.
Excellent: neat, accurate work that fits first time; explains each step and checks every coupling and bracket for firmness.
observables: Holds metal conduit in a pipe vice and cuts the threads with a die set
Threads are clean and full, and the coupling screws on fully with the conduits in line
Support bracket or saddle is fixed firmly and the conduit does not move when pushed
pcs.observablesSource: Derived from the PC text

pcs.text: use appropriate electrical measuring devices like ammmeter, voltmeter,meggers etc.to examine electrical units for power interruptions/ continuity
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses the wrong instrument or range, tests continuity on a live circuit, or misreads the value.
Meets standard: selects the right instrument and range, tests safely and reads correctly whether supply or continuity is present.
Exceeds in places: also proves the meter on a known source before and after testing, and traces the break to a specific point.
Excellent: uses all instruments confidently and safely, explains what each reading means, and records results clearly.
observables: Picks the right instrument: voltmeter or multimeter for supply, continuity tester for breaks, megger for insulation
Sets the function and range before connecting the leads
Checks continuity only with the supply switched off
Reads the value correctly and says whether supply or continuity is present
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 13
synonyms: लाइन आ रही है कि नहीं

pcs.text: use electrical devices such as starters, circuit breakers, relays as per equipment/ wiring installation rating or current rating
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or picks a device without reading its rating, or one too large or too small for the circuit.
Meets standard: reads labels, chooses a breaker, starter or relay of the rating in the drawing or for the load, and wires it correctly.
Exceeds in places: explains why that rating suits the load and wire size, and checks pole count and type before fitting.
Excellent: selects and fits all devices correctly without help, explains each one's job and spots a wrongly rated device.
observables: Reads the rating label (current, poles, voltage) on the breaker, starter or relay
Chosen device rating matches the drawing or the load it serves
Device is mounted and wired to its marked line and load terminals
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: use diagnostic devices like multi-meter, tong tester, earth tester or similar devices to install, repair power connections
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or wrong meter setting, clamps the whole cable, touches live parts, or cannot read the meter.
Meets standard: measures voltage and load current correctly with multimeter and tong tester and uses the readings to check the connection.
Exceeds in places: also uses the earth tester as its instructions say and compares readings with expected values to judge the work.
Excellent: confident, safe use of all devices; explains each reading, finds the problem from them and records results neatly.
observables: Measures voltage at the connection with the multimeter set to AC volts
Clamps the tong tester around one conductor only to read the load current
Notes each reading with its unit and packs the instrument away after use
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: perform maintenance and upkeep of relevant tools and devices after use
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or tools are left dirty or scattered, or damaged tools are mixed in with good ones.
Meets standard: cleans tools and devices after use and stores them in the proper place, with sharp tools covered or boxed.
Exceeds in places: also checks tools for damage while cleaning, tags or reports faulty ones, and coils cables neatly.
Excellent: thorough upkeep as routine: tools cleaned, checked, counted and stored in order, ready for the next job.
observables: Cleans dust and debris off tools and instruments after use
Returns tools to the tool box or set place, with sharp tools stored safely
Coils power tool cables and switches meters off before storing them
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

nos.title: Install temporary lighting arrangement at construction sites

elements.title: Installation of temporary lighting arrangement at construction sites

pcs.text: check cable, conduits , lights, sockets, temporary power distribution panels at power source and other required fixtures and accessories as per manufacturers guidelines and specification
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses items without checking, such as a damaged cable, wrong size wire or wrongly rated MCB.
Meets standard: checks cable, conduits, lights, sockets, MCBs and the temporary DB for rating, size and damage before use.
Exceeds in places: checks labels and markings against the manufacturer's specification and plans the shortest safe routing.
Excellent: complete, orderly check of every item, with faulty items set aside and reported; explains why each check matters.
observables: Checks cable and wire size and type against the requirement and looks for damage
Checks switches, sockets and MCBs for the needed rating and condition
Checks lights and fittings for damage and the correct type before installing
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: lay cables through ducts or conduits, underground or through poles (overhead) as per plans and instructions
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cable is dragged, kinked or laid in an unchecked trench, or left unprotected across paths.
Meets standard: checks the trench, lays the cable along the planned route without damage and protects it where it crosses or rises.
Exceeds in places: keeps the cable straight with gentle bends and marks the buried route so others know where it runs.
Excellent: neat, damage free laying exactly as planned; route marked and protected, and the method explained clearly.
observables: Checks trench depth and width and looks for existing underground services before laying
Lays the cable without sharp bends, twists or dragging over sharp edges
Cable is protected in a pipe or duct where it crosses a path or rises from the ground
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: select the type and wattage of lights considering illumination requirement at worksite and install them at secured positions
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or wrong type or wattage, or the light is left loose, too low, or aimed away from the work.
Meets standard: picks the type and wattage in the drawing and fixes the light securely where it lights the work area.
Exceeds in places: explains the choice from the area and task, and aims lights to avoid dark spots and glare in workers' eyes.
Excellent: selection and placement give even, glare free light; fixtures rigid and safe, and choices explained with reasons.
observables: Selects the light type and wattage given in the drawing or instruction
Light is mounted firmly at a height and angle that lights the work area
Fixture and its cable are secured so they cannot fall or be knocked
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: fix lights and its accessories, brackets, bulkheads with screws and bolts or by other standard means, pull wires through conduit leading to connection boxes, temporary panels/ distribution boards or other temporary electrical terminals
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the fitting is loose, wires are scraped or forced, or the cable is left unconnected or misconnected.
Meets standard: fixes lights and brackets firmly, pulls wires cleanly through conduit and connects them at the box or DB.
Exceeds in places: fixings are level and evenly tightened, wires have neat spare length and the cable is clamped at entry.
Excellent: neat, rigid installation done in a logical order; all connections right first time and checked before switching on.
observables: Light and bracket are fixed with screws, bolts or clamps and do not move when pushed
Pulls wires through the conduit to the junction box or DB without scraping the insulation
Routes the cable to the distribution board and connects it to the correct outgoing terminal
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: extend/ join LV electrical cable using straight through joints, splicing them together and secure joints by applying PVC insulation tapes, caps or by other safe method as and when necessary
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cores are nicked, mismatched or loosely joined, or copper is left exposed after taping.
Meets standard: strips cleanly, joins matching cores tightly and insulates each core joint and the whole joint fully.
Exceeds in places: staggers the core joints to keep the joint slim and tapes with even overlap carried over the sheath.
Excellent: neat, strong, fully sealed joint done to standard practice; tests continuity or insulation after jointing.
observables: Removes sheath and insulation with the right tool without cutting conductor strands
Joins each core tightly to its matching core
Each core joint and then the whole joint is insulated with PVC tape or a sleeve, no copper showing
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: carry out termination of LV cables selecting the right method as per standard practice
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or stray strands, bare copper outside the terminal, a loose screw, or a lug that is not crimped.
Meets standard: chooses a suitable termination method, strips correctly, crimps lugs where needed and tightens the terminals.
Exceeds in places: uses lugs and glands of the right size, follows the sequence neatly and tug-tests every termination.
Excellent: all terminations neat, tight and correctly sized first time; explains why loose terminations overheat.
observables: Strips the conductor to the length the terminal needs, with no bare copper outside it
Uses a lug crimped with a crimping tool, or a cable gland, where the method needs one
Follows the sequence: strip, fit lug or ferrule, insert, tighten, then check by tugging
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: work safely as per electrical safety guidelines provided by manufacturer, standard safety practice or organizational safety norms while establishing or disconnecting live electrical connections
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or works on live parts without isolating and testing dead, or without gloves and insulated tools.
Meets standard: isolates the supply, tests dead, uses insulated tools and PPE, and restores supply only when the work is complete.
Exceeds in places: also locks or tags the isolating switch and warns others before switching off and back on.
Excellent: safe practice throughout without prompting; isolates, proves dead, tags, and explains each safety step.
observables: Switches off and isolates the supply before connecting or disconnecting
Tests that the circuit is dead with a tester before touching the conductors
Wears insulated gloves and safety shoes and uses insulated tools
Stands on a dry surface or rubber mat, away from water
pcs.observablesSource: Derived from the PC text

pcs.text: upkeep of all relevant key electrical tools and fixtures
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or tools and fittings are left dirty, wet or scattered, or damaged items are mixed with good ones.
Meets standard: cleans tools and fixtures after use, stores them in a dry set place and reports damaged items.
Exceeds in places: also checks items while storing, keeps spares sorted by type and rating, and coils cables neatly.
Excellent: tools and fixtures kept clean, checked and orderly as routine, so the next job starts without delay.
observables: Cleans tools and spare fittings after use
Stores tools and fixtures in a dry, safe, set place
Keeps damaged tools or fixtures apart and reports them
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: tag embedded, exposed electrical lines and other key equipment appropriately
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or lines and equipment are left untagged, tags cannot be read, or there is no caution board at the DB.
Meets standard: tags exposed and embedded lines and key equipment with readable tags and puts a caution board near the DB.
Exceeds in places: tags state the circuit and source clearly, are fixed durably, and buried routes are marked at the surface.
Excellent: complete, consistent tagging that anyone on site can follow; explains how tags prevent accidents.
observables: Tags are fixed on exposed and embedded cable routes and can be read
Caution board is displayed near the distribution board
Tags name the circuit or equipment and are placed where they can be seen
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: shift light at various locations during construction activity as per requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or shifts the light live, leaves cable on the ground or sagging, or leaves the fixture loose.
Meets standard: switches off, shifts the light, runs cable on supports at least 2 m high, ties it, then tests after reconnecting.
Exceeds in places: chooses the shortest safe route, keeps the cable taut without over sagging, and secures the fixture firmly.
Excellent: quick, tidy shift with no hazard left behind; cable neatly tied, light aimed well and working at first switch-on.
observables: Chooses a short and safe route for the cable
Routes the cable on supports and ties it at every vertical support
Cable runs not less than 2 m above ground level
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: repair and replace light arrangements as per instruction or requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or opens the fitting live, leaves screws or cover missing, or the light still does not work.
Meets standard: isolates, opens the fitting, replaces the faulty part, reassembles fully and confirms the light works.
Exceeds in places: finds the actual fault before replacing, so only the faulty part is changed, and seals the fitting properly.
Excellent: safe, quick repair done in the right order; fitting left clean and sealed, and the fault and fix explained.
observables: Switches off and disconnects the cable before opening the fitting
Removes the screws, opens the light case and replaces the damaged part
Reassembles the case with all screws and checks that the light works
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: replace burned out bulbs, light units and ballast in light fixtures as needed
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or changes the bulb live, fits a part of a different type or wattage, or leaves the cover off.
Meets standard: isolates, replaces the bulb, choke or driver with one of the same configuration and checks that the light works.
Exceeds in places: reads the old part's markings before getting a replacement and handles fragile lamps without breakage.
Excellent: safe, quick, correct replacement; disposes of the old lamp properly and explains why matching ratings matter.
observables: Switches off and disconnects before touching the fitting
New bulb, choke (ballast) or LED driver matches the old one in type, wattage and voltage
Reassembles the fitting and checks that the light works
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: carry out relevant tests to trace out power interruptions/ continuity at lighting arrangements
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or wrong meter setting, continuity tested live, or the break in supply is not found.
Meets standard: checks voltage and continuity with a test lamp or correctly set multimeter and finds where supply is lost.
Exceeds in places: tests in a logical order from source to light and narrows the fault to one joint, switch or fitting.
Excellent: fast, safe and systematic; pinpoints the fault, explains the readings and confirms supply after the repair.
observables: Checks continuity of the circuit with a test lamp or multimeter, supply off
Measures supply voltage at the fitting with the multimeter on the AC voltage range
Multimeter knob is set to the right function before the probes touch the circuit
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15
synonyms: सप्लाई आ रही है या नहीं

pcs.text: replace damaged cable, other relevant parts as and when necessary
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or works live, leaves damaged cable in place, uses a different size, or leaves the joint bare.
Meets standard: isolates, cuts out the damaged part, joins in matching cable properly, tapes the joint and tags it.
Exceeds in places: replaces the full damaged length to avoid extra joints and tests continuity or insulation before re-energising.
Excellent: neat, safe repair with the fewest joints, tested and tagged; explains what caused the damage and how to prevent it.
observables: Identifies the damaged portion of cable and cuts it out with the right tools
Splices in cable of the same size and type by the proper method
Protects the joint with PVC insulation tape and tags it for identification
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: replace faulty circuit breakers, fuses, switches, electrical and electronic components and wire as per requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or replaces with supply on, fits a different rating, or swaps load and supply wires.
Meets standard: isolates the mains, removes the faulty part, fits one of the same rating, reconnects correctly and checks operation.
Exceeds in places: notes wire positions before removal, uses the right fuse wire or cartridge and tightens all terminals evenly.
Excellent: safe, orderly replacement right first time; finds why the part failed and explains it to the supervisor.
observables: Switches off the mains and disconnects the load before removing the faulty part
New breaker, fuse or switch has the same rating and type as the one removed
Load and supply wires go back on the correct terminals and are tightened
Supply is restored and operation is checked
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: perform preventive maintenance on diesel generators at site provided for temporary lighting (if any) at scheduled intervals as per direction of concerned authority
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or checks levels on a running or hot engine, opens a hot radiator cap, or skips checks and records.
Meets standard: checks fuel, oil and coolant levels, watches noise and smoke, reads the meters and records it as directed.
Exceeds in places: also looks for leaks and loose connections and reports overload or under load readings to the supervisor.
Excellent: complete, safe routine done at the scheduled interval; log kept accurately and early warning signs reported.
observables: Checks fuel, lubricating oil and coolant levels with the engine stopped and cool
Watches the running set for unusual noise or smoke and reads the load and power factor meters
Records the checks in the DG log or inspection record
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 35

nos.title: Assist in LV (Low Voltage) electrical wiring at permanent structures

elements.title: Provide assistance for LV electrical wiring work in permanent structures

pcs.text: select house wiring components (such as wires flexible and rigid conduits, PVC raceways wooden battens, clamps etc according to their specification size
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or picks wire, conduit or accessories of the wrong size or type for the drawing.
Meets standard: selects wires, conduits and accessories of the size and type in the drawing, checking the markings on each.
Exceeds in places: checks quality marks and condition, and picks matching bends, boxes and clamps so parts fit without rework.
Excellent: complete, correct selection without help; explains why each size suits the load and spots wrong items.
observables: Selected wire size matches the drawing, checked from the marking on the coil
Conduit type and diameter match the drawing
Boxes, bends, clamps or battens chosen fit the selected conduit
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: read and interpret single phase LV wiring diagram
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cannot read the symbols, or places points or routing differently from the drawing.
Meets standard: reads the symbols, follows the routing sequence and the conduit and wire sizes, and places points as drawn.
Exceeds in places: explains how each switch controls its light and spots missing or unclear details to ask about.
Excellent: reads the diagram fluently and explains the full circuit, including the phase, neutral and earth paths.
observables: Identifies the symbols for switch, socket, light, fan and DB in the drawing
Traces the route from the DB to each point and states the conduit and wire size given
Points out on the wall where each switch, socket and fixture goes as per the drawing
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: carry out necessary linear measurement to cut bend join conduits and cables and use them as per requirement or instruction
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or no marking, cuts by guess so pieces are short or wasted, or marks differ from the drawing.
Meets standard: marks points and route as per the drawing, measures the runs and cuts conduit and cable to the needed lengths.
Exceeds in places: uses level and plumb lines for marking, allows for bends and spare wire, and wastes very little material.
Excellent: accurate marking and cutting that fit first time with almost no waste; checks measurements twice before cutting.
observables: Marks the fixture locations and the conduit route on the wall as per the drawing
Measures each run with a tape before cutting conduit or cable
Cuts conduits and wires to the required size with the correct tools
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: lay conduit through RCC structures (slabs beams walls) or through chased wall (brick wall) surface as per instruction
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the route differs from the drawing, conduit sticks out of the chase, or joints are open.
Meets standard: lays and fixes conduit as per the drawing with straight runs, closed joints and ends terminating in boxes.
Exceeds in places: keeps runs neat and parallel, uses smooth bends instead of sharp joints, and fixes conduit firmly before plastering.
Excellent: clean, accurate conduit layout matching the drawing exactly; open ends capped against concrete and debris.
observables: Conduit is placed and fixed along the route shown in the drawing
Runs are straight, horizontal or vertical, and end in boxes
Conduit sits fully inside the chase, below the plaster line
Joints use couplers and bends, with no open gaps
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: lock conduit pipe in its location by means of clamp or other standard means as per instruction
pcs.measurementTask: Measure the largest gap between consecutive saddles or clamps on the conduit run the candidate fixed.
observables: Saddles or clamps are fixed along the whole conduit run
Each saddle grips the conduit tightly, with screws in wall plugs
Conduit does not move or sag between supports
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16: Provide support by fixing the saddles at 500 mm spacing.

pcs.text: pull, push wires through conduits in order to expose them at desired locations as per requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or wires are forced so insulation tears or kinks, or wires end too short at the boxes.
Meets standard: uses a fish wire or spring to pull the wires through together without damage, leaving spare length at boxes.
Exceeds in places: keeps the wire coil from twisting, pulls steadily with a helper feeding, and leaves even, neat spare ends.
Excellent: smooth, damage free pulling on the first attempt; wires identified at both ends and conduit not overfilled.
observables: Uses a GI fish wire or steel spring to draw the wires through the conduit
Pulls the circuit's wires together without forcing, scraping or kinking the insulation
Wires come out at each box with enough spare length to terminate
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Assistant Electrician (CON/Q0602 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: perform drilling and cutting using appropriate tools as per requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cuts without PPE, off the marked line, or too deep or into RCC members, damaging the structure.
Meets standard: chases and drills at the marked positions with the right tool and PPE, with grooves that fit the conduit.
Exceeds in places: grooves are straight and uniform at the correct depth, wall damage is minimal and dust is kept down.
Excellent: clean, accurate chasing and drilling done safely and quickly, with full control of the tool throughout.
observables: Cuts the groove in the masonry wall along the marked line with a chasing machine
Wears goggles, dust mask and gloves while chasing or drilling
Groove depth and width suit the conduit, and holes are drilled at the marked points
